The features of CensusMapper's base map as sf data

Source: R/cm_helpers.R
cm_context.Rd

Gets the features of CensusMapper's base map for the extent of some sf data or a bounding box from CensusMapper's vector tiles: water, landcover, landuse, airports, buildings, roads, and places and road labels. These are the features geom_cm_context() draws, unstyled, for drawing them in other ways or with other mapping packages.

Usage

cm_context(
  data,
  layers = c("water", "landcover", "landuse", "aeroway", "buildings", "roads", "places",
    "road_labels"),
  zoom = NULL,
  pixels = 800,
  language = getOption("cancensus.language", "en"),
  tile_server = "https://censusmapper.ca",
  api_key = Sys.getenv("CM_API_KEY")
)

Arguments

data

sf data, an sfc or a bounding box whose extent to get the base map for.

layers

Which layers to get, any of "water", "landcover", "landuse", "aeroway", "buildings", "roads", "places" and "road_labels".

zoom

Zoom level (as on CensusMapper) whose tiles to use. By default the zoom level at which the data spans pixels pixels.

pixels

The width, in pixels, of the CensusMapper map whose zoom level to use.

language

Language of the names, "en" or "fr". Defaults to the cancensus.language option, and to "en" if that is not set.

tile_server

Where to get the tiles from.

api_key

An API key for the CensusMapper API. Defaults to the CM_API_KEY environment variable, as set with set_cancensus_api_key().

Value

A named list with an sf data frame for each layer, in the CRS of data and cropped to its bounding box. A layer without features is an sf data frame without rows. Features have their class, and places and road labels their name in the language language (or the local name). Road labels are points along named roads, with the angle (in degrees) to turn labels by and the length of the road (in metres). The other columns come from the tiles and may change. The zoom level is in the "zoom" attribute.

Details

The tiles, and with them the detail of the features, are those CensusMapper uses at the zoom level at which the data spans pixels pixels, or at zoom. Which classes of features exist at a zoom level is decided by the tiles; geom_cm_context() additionally shows some classes (minor roads, buildings, road labels) only at higher zoom levels.

Tiles are downloaded from the tile server and cached for the session. They need a CensusMapper API key, the same as for the census data, though tiles count against a separate tile quota. Needs GDAL with its MVT driver for sf to read the tiles.

See also

geom_cm_context() to add the base map to a ggplot map.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
library(ggplot2)
census_data <- get_census("CA21", regions = list(CSD = "5915022"),
                          vectors = c(population = "v_CA21_1"),
                          level = "DA", geo_format = "sf")
context <- cm_context(census_data, layers = c("water", "roads", "places"))
major <- context$roads[context$roads$class %in% c("motorway", "trunk", "primary"), ]
ggplot(census_data) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = population / `Shape Area`), colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = context$water, fill = "lightblue", colour = NA) +
  geom_sf(data = major, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_sf_text(data = context$places[context$places$class == "suburb", ],
               aes(label = name), size = 3) +
  coord_sf(datum = NA)
} # }
